questions.q: Which network device broadcasts received data to all connected ports without any addressing intelligence?
questions.solution: A hub is a multi-port repeater - it blindly repeats every bit to every port. Switches consult a MAC table; routers consult IP routes.
questions.shortcut: Dumb broadcast = hub; smart selection = switch.

questions.q: The keyboard shortcut to increase the indent of a paragraph in MS Word is:
questions.solution: Ctrl+M increases indent, Ctrl+Shift+M decreases it. (Tab indents only at the start of a paragraph/list item; Ctrl+I is italic.)
questions.shortcut: M = More indent; add Shift = less.

questions.q: PARAM 8000, India's first indigenous supercomputer (1991), was developed by:
questions.solution: PARAM 8000 was built in 1991 by C-DAC (Centre for Development of Advanced Computing), Pune, under Dr Vijay Bhatkar, after the USA denied Cray supercomputer imports.
questions.shortcut: PARAM always pairs with C-DAC; the denial story (' PARAM = Perform Anvaya Reusable Module') is extra trivia - the developer is what SSC asks.

questions.q: An attacker who secretly relays and possibly alters communication between a user and a banking site is performing a:
questions.solution: In MITM the attacker sits between the two endpoints, intercepting/relaying traffic - a classic danger of unencrypted links and open Wi-Fi.
questions.shortcut: Secretly standing between two parties = man-in-the-middle.

questions.q:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

To hit the nail on the head
options: to state exactly the right thing
questions.solution: One clean, accurate blow — a description or answer perfectly on target → **to speak with exact correctness**.
questions.shortcut: Accuracy picture: the blow lands precisely.

questions.q:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The company had to call ___ the proposed merger after the audit report.
questions.solution: Action = cancel: **call off**. *Call up* telephones, *call out* challenges/announces, *call for* demands — none survives the substitution test.
questions.shortcut: Substitute 'cancel' — the surviving particle is off.

questions.q:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

To make both ends meet
questions.solution: One's two 'ends' — income and expense — must touch: **to manage on a limited income**. Ropes, tasks and friendships are literal decoys for 'ends'.
questions.shortcut: Ends = income and expense; making them meet = balancing a budget.

questions.q:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Achilles' heel
options: a weak point despite overall strength
questions.solution: The hero Achilles was invulnerable except where his mother held him — his heel. Hence **the one weakness in a strong person or system**.
questions.shortcut: Allusion anchor: the great hero's single vulnerable spot.

questions.q: The classical dance **Kuchipudi** takes its name from a village in which state?
questions.solution: Kuchipudi village is in the **Krishna district of Andhra Pradesh**. The dance is known for *Tarangam*, performed on the rim of a brass plate.

questions.q: The revised Wholesale Price Index series released in June 2026 is characterised by:
options: inclusion of services in the headline WPI
an expanded basket of 957 items (from 697) alongside the launch of Producer Price Indices
a shift of compilation from DPIIT to NSO
questions.solution: DPIIT's Office of Economic Adviser launched the WPI **2022-23 series on 15 June 2026**, expanding the basket from **697 to 957 items** and releasing new **Producer Price Indices**; WPI will run beside PPI for five years. Services remain outside headline WPI, and compilation stays with DPIIT.
questions.shortcut: Basket 697→957 and PPI twins — both changed together.

questions.q: Which is the highest peak of South India?
questions.solution: **Anamudi** (2,695 m) in the Anaimalai Hills of Kerala is the highest peak of South India. Doddabetta is the highest in the Nilgiris; Guru Shikhar is the highest in the Aravallis (Rajasthan).
questions.shortcut: 'Ana-mudi' — the 'elephant's forehead' stands tallest in the south.

questions.q: Which metal is stored under kerosene to prevent it from reacting with air and moisture?
questions.solution: **Sodium** (and potassium) react vigorously with oxygen and water — sodium can catch fire — so they are kept **under kerosene**. White phosphorus, a non-metal, is stored under water.

questions.q: A boat's downstream speed is 20 km/h and its upstream speed is 12 km/h. The speed of the boat in still water is:
questions.solution: $b = \frac{20 + 12}{2} = 16$ km/h (stream = 4 km/h).

questions.q: An alloy of 40 grams contains zinc and copper in the ratio 5 : 3. How much copper must be added so that the ratio becomes 5 : 7?
questions.solution: Zinc 25 g, copper 15 g. Want $\frac{25}{15 + x} = \frac{5}{7}$ ⇒ $15 + x = 35$ ⇒ $x = 20$ g.
questions.shortcut: Zinc constant 25; copper must reach 35 ⇒ add 20 g.

questions.q: What is the product of the place values of the two 3s in 53,432?
questions.solution: In 53,432 the first 3 is in the thousands place (3000) and the second is in the tens place (30). Product $= 3000 \times 30 = 90,000$.

questions.q: The average age of a husband and wife at the time of their marriage was 23 years. After 5 years they have a one-year-old child. The average age of the family of three now is:
questions.solution:
Marriage total = 2 × 23 = 46. After 5 years: 46 + 5 + 5 = 56.
Child adds 1 year: total = 57.
Average $= \frac{57}{3} = 19$ years.
questions.shortcut: Both adults age 5 (total 56), child is 1 ⇒ 57/3 = 19. (Trap: forgetting to add the child's own age.)

questions.q: What is the position of the letter **W from the right** of the English alphabet?
questions.solution: W = 23 from the left → 27 − 23 = **4th** from the right (Z 1st, Y 2nd, X 3rd, W 4th).

questions.q: Four married couples — **(A, P), (B, Q), (C, R), (D, S)** — sit around a circular table facing the centre. **C sits opposite A; B opposite P; S opposite Q. R is to the immediate left of A, Q to the immediate left of P, and D to the immediate left of C. Q is an immediate neighbour of A.** Who sits **opposite R**?
questions.solution: Fix P anywhere: Q at P's left; B opposite P; S opposite Q. Q must touch A, and R sits at A's left with C opposite A and D at C's left — the string P, Q, A, R, B, S, C, D closes the circle. R, three... four seats across (8 seats → +4) faces **D**.
questions.shortcut: Spouses opposite + left-neighbour chains: lay the 8-string down once, then read +4.

questions.q: Which diagram correctly represents **Mothers, Females and Engineers**?
options: Mothers inside Females; Engineers circle intersecting both
questions.solution: Every mother is definitionally a female → Mothers inside Females. Engineers can be male or female and may or may not be mothers → the Engineers circle crosses both.
questions.shortcut: Definition decides nesting; possibility decides intersection.
